Solutions 1 and 2 are wrong because $\mathrm{sd}_\iota(P_6)=4$. The path $P_n$ has $\iota(P_n)=\lceil (n-1)/4\rceil$. A set of $k$ vertices covers at most $3k$ vertices, and the uncovered vertices form at most $k+1$ segments, each of size at most 1. So $\iota(P_6)=2$, and $\iota(P_9)=2$ via $S=\{3,7\}$. For $P_{10}$, two vertices leave at least 4 uncovered vertices in at most 3 segments of size at most 1, so $\iota(P_{10})=3$. Subdividing 4 of the 5 edges of $P_6$ gives $P_{10}$, and 3 subdivisions give $P_9$, so $\mathrm{sd}_\iota(P_6)=4$. This rules out 3 and 2 as the maximum.

Solution 3 reaches 5 using the formula $\iota(P_n)=\lceil n/5\rceil$, which is incorrect, so its argument does not support 5. I could not verify that any tree attains 5, and none of the three solutions gives 4, which is the only value I have verified as attained.

CHOICE: NONE
CONFIDENCE: 3
